Architecture, transaction-boundary, state-machine, security-filter-design and deployability lens. graphify-out/graph.json is NOT present in the RC (only graphify-out/cache/ exists) — `graphify query` fails with 'graph file not found', so every citation below was opened and traced directly in source, not via graph.
agreements: EV-001 — confirmed at TrendPullJob.java:156 (public 5-arg ctor, delegates via this(...)) and :175 (package-private 7-arg ctor). Neither is @Autowired and the class is @Component (line 33 import, verified @Component/@Scheduled/@SchedulerLock present on the class). Two non-annotated constructors on a Spring-managed bean is a hard BeanCreationException at context refresh, in every profile — this is not conditional on any env var, so it independently blocks even the fix for EV-013.

EV-002 — confirmed EscrowService.initiateFund (200-341) has no requireStatus/status check on an existing FUNDED/RELEASED/REFUNDED milestone before creating a new hold and calling applyFunding; only assertContractActiveForMilestone (388-430) runs, which checks contract signatures and collaboration-cancelled state only. By contrast I verified release/releaseByHoldId (623-690) and refund (945-1015) both DO call requireStatus(hold, EscrowStatus.FUNDED, ...) after a locked read (requireHoldForUpdate). This proves EV-002 is a genuine, isolated omission on initiateFund specifically — every sibling money-moving method in the same class enforces the state-machine guard that initiateFund skips.

EV-003 — confirmed the exact transaction shape: WalletService.requestCreatorWithdrawal (249) is @Transactional and takes a pessimistic wallet lock (findByOwnerIdForUpdate, 263); doProcessWithdrawal (381) is self-invoked via lambda so its own @Transactional is inert and it runs inside the SAME ambient transaction; ledgerService.post locks the platform clearing wallet FOR UPDATE; razorpayXClient.initiatePayout (a real blocking HTTP call) runs next, still inside that transaction, with the wallet+clearing-wallet locks held; payoutRepository.save happens only after. Independently confirmed IdempotencyService's class javadoc (lines 33-60) documents that markCompleted was deliberately moved to a separate REQUIRES_NEW bean (IdempotencyReservationOps) specifically so it commits durably and independently of the caller's ambient transaction — which means the idempotency-COMPLETED write is guaranteed durable before the outer withdrawal transaction commits, exactly as EV-003 states. Also confirmed RazorpayXClient's shared HttpClient only sets connectTimeout(10s) (RazorpayXClient.java ~line 27) with no per-request .timeout() on the built HttpRequest, so a hung RazorpayX response holds both row locks indefinitely, not just for 10s.

EV-004 — confirmed InternalServiceTokenFilter.doFilterInternal (82-86) gates only on `stripContext(request.getRequestURI()).startsWith("/internal/")` using the RAW (undecoded) URI. Confirmed SecurityConfig has no `.requestMatchers("/internal/**")` rule at all — /internal/** falls through to the generic `.anyRequest().authenticated()` (SecurityConfig ~297-304), so once this filter no-ops on an encoded path it is not any special exemption, it's ordinary human-JWT-authenticated access to MeeraInternalController's @RequestMapping("/internal/meera") (line 74) endpoints. See XR-PRIYA-01 below for why this is worse than a one-off oversight.

EV-005 — confirmed CampaignWriteRequest.status (CampaignDtos, line 64) is a plain client-settable field bound directly by @RequestBody on the public create endpoint, and CampaignService.create (145-235) calls validator.validateStatusForWorkspace(status, workspace), which I opened at CampaignValidator.java:62-69 — it only checks workspace.getVerificationStatus() == VERIFIED, nothing about escrow funding or the publish fee. create() never calls requireFundedEscrow or chargeOnPublish anywhere in its body, unlike update()'s transitioningToActive branch (360-378) which calls both. A verified brand can POST /campaigns with status=ACTIVE directly.

EV-009 — confirmed Dockerfile:65 runs `RUN npx vite build` directly, not `npm run build`; package.json's postbuild hook (`node scripts/generate-sitemap.mjs && node scripts/prerender.mjs`, package.json line 8) only fires for `npm run build`, so it is structurally skipped in the image build, matching the Dockerfile's own comment at lines 65-67 admitting this and leaving a TODO(prod). Also independently confirmed VITE_PAYOUTS_ENABLED=false is baked in as an ARG/ENV default (Dockerfile ~line 58), corroborating EV-020's 'withdraw off by default' claim from the same file.

EV-010 — I am a co-source on this finding from an earlier pass; re-confirmed on this pass that no add_header Content-Security-Policy exists in deploy/utho/nginx-influora.conf, deploy/utho/nginx-influora-app.conf, or deploy/hostinger/Caddyfile.

EV-011 — confirmed WalletTransactionType.AFFILIATE_COMMISSION and TxnReferenceType.AFFILIATE_EARNING exist as Java enum constants but V8__wallet_transactions.sql's `type` and `reference_type` MySQL ENUM column definitions (lines 6-12) do not list either value, and no later migration file widens them (grep across influora-api/src/main/resources/db/migration for AFFILIATE_COMMISSION returns zero migration hits). Any INSERT using these Java enum values will fail against a real (non-lenient) MySQL column.

EV-014 — confirmed the arithmetic: scopedKey = "creator-withdraw:" (17 chars) + userId (26-char ULID) + ":" (1) + idempotencyKey, built at WalletService.java:304. A standard 36-char UUID header pushes the key to 80 chars against `idempotency_key VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL UNIQUE` (V8__wallet_transactions.sql:15). No sql_mode override exists in either compose file, so MySQL 8's default STRICT_TRANS_TABLES applies and this is a hard INSERT failure, not silent truncation — every real-UUID-header withdrawal fails at commit.

EV-017 — confirmed more strongly than the register states: influora-api/src/main/resources/application.yml has ZERO `spring.data.redis.*` keys anywhere in the file (grep for 'redis' case-insensitively returns only a comment at line 181), and no Java class reads a `REDIS_URL` env var (zero hits repo-wide). Setting `REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379` in the compose files' environment block, as both deploy/hostinger and deploy/utho do, has no effect on Spring's Redis autoconfiguration, which binds `spring.data.redis.host`/`port`/`url` — none of which is set by relaxed-binding from a var named REDIS_URL. Spring Boot's Redis autoconfig falls back to its hardcoded localhost:6379 default, which inside the influora-api container resolves to the container's own loopback, not the `redis` compose service.

EV-020 — confirmed via Dockerfile ARG/ENV VITE_PAYOUTS_ENABLED=false default and independently corroborates the AdminFinanceService manual-UTR payout path (admin/AdminFinanceService.java, @Transactional at line 149 documented as 'does not move money: a human enters the UTR').

disagreements.position: Evidence score should be E3-E4, not the claimed E5, given the rubric's own definition.
disagreements.evidence: The register's own reproduction field says 'Static: follow the call chain above... not performed' — no runtime/Testcontainers reproduction exists for this finding. The stated evidence_score rubric reserves 5 for 'multiple independent sources (code+runtime, code+test, two agents reproduce)'. Two agents independently reading the same source and reaching the same conclusion is a real corroboration signal (and I independently re-traced the same chain and agree with the conclusion), but it is still a single evidence *type* (code), not two independent evidence types. I would not block on this — the underlying defect is real and I've verified it myself — but the score inflates confidence beyond what static analysis alone should carry, especially since 'commit-time failure after the gateway call succeeds' is the load-bearing trigger condition and that specific interleaving has not been reproduced.
disagreements.proposed_change: Re-score EV-003 evidence_score to 3 (code + reproducible path via clear call-chain tracing) rather than 5, and add a verification_required action to actually run the Testcontainers repro already specified in the register's own verification_required field before this is treated as launch-blocking-confirmed rather than launch-blocking-highly-likely.

missing_evidence: EV-013 (TrendPullJob disabled by missing TREND_INGEST_CLASSIFIER_WORKSPACE_ID) is scoped as a configuration/feature-flag gap, but EV-001 (boot failure on the same class, TrendPullJob) means the config gap is currently unobservable in practice — the application cannot reach a state where TrendPullJob's config-gated behavior would even run. The register does not cross-reference these two findings against each other; a reader could fix EV-013's env var and still get zero trend ingestion because EV-001 prevents the JVM from starting at all. Recommend EV-013 explicitly note 'blocked by EV-001; re-verify after EV-001 is fixed' rather than being read as an independent, separately-actionable P1.

missed_issues.title: The exact percent-encoding path-bypass vulnerability class in EV-004 was already found and fixed in a sibling filter (AuthRateLimitFilter) but the fix was never applied to InternalServiceTokenFilter, the most security-critical filter in the app
missed_issues.evidence: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/security/AuthRateLimitFilter.java carries an explicit code comment block (lines 69-71, repeated at 620-623, attributed '[Kabir NEW-1]') stating: 'HttpServletRequest#getRequestURI() returns the RAW, undecoded path; a request for /wallet/%77ithdraw would otherwise silently bypass every literal-path bucket match here' — and its bucketFor method (line 343) is implemented as `decode(stripContext(request.getRequestURI()))`, i.e. it decodes before matching. InternalServiceTokenFilter.java (the filter EV-004 is about) does the exact opposite at line 82-83: `String path = stripContext(request.getRequestURI()); if (!path.startsWith(INTERNAL_PREFIX))` — no decode() call anywhere in the file. This is not an isolated oversight nobody in this codebase understood; it is a known, named, already-fixed vulnerability class (present in the code, with the fixer's own name on the comment) that a second, more security-sensitive filter guarding the machine-to-machine (Meera AI service) trust boundary never received.
missed_issues.location: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/security/InternalServiceTokenFilter.java:82-83 (no decode) vs influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/security/AuthRateLimitFilter.java:69-71,343,620-623 (decode() applied, with the vulnerability explicitly documented)
missed_issues.impact: This elevates EV-004 from 'a bug in one filter' to 'a missing cross-cutting invariant': the codebase has no shared utility/base class enforcing decoded-path matching across all path-prefix security filters, and no test asserting every filter under security/ that gates by path prefix uses the decoded form. A future filter (and this one specifically, the highest-trust one) can and did regress past a fix that already exists two files away. Fixing InternalServiceTokenFilter alone (as EV-004's recommended_fix proposes) does not close the systemic gap — the next filter added to this package can reintroduce the exact same class of bug with no test catching it.
missed_issues.recommended_fix: Extract AuthRateLimitFilter's decode()/stripMatrixParams()/stripContext() helpers into a shared PathNormalizer (or equivalent) used by every OncePerRequestFilter in security/ that does prefix/path matching (InternalServiceTokenFilter, AuthRateLimitFilter, AnalyticsUsageCapInterceptor), and add an architecture test (ArchUnit or a simple reflection-based test) that fails if a class in that package calls request.getRequestURI() without routing it through the shared decoder — so this class of regression is caught at build time, not by the next red-team pass.
missed_issues.verification_required: After the shared decoder lands, add a unit test sending a percent-encoded path variant of /internal/meera/messages (e.g. /api/v1/%69nternal/meera/messages) through the full filter chain in a @WebMvcTest/@SpringBootTest slice and assert it is rejected with 401/403, not routed to MeeraInternalController.

missed_issues.title: influora-api has no non-Docker, no-DB-required Spring context smoke test, so the EV-001 boot failure (and any future one like it) is structurally invisible to CI/local `mvn test`
missed_issues.evidence: meera-run's own reproduction (cited in EV-001) needed a live migrated MySQL under SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=dev to even reach the point of failure (Flyway validated 136 migrations, Hibernate context built, THEN the bean-creation exception surfaced at singleton pre-instantiation). Per this repo's own working memory (reference_local_mvn_test_skips_docker_tests.md), the only full-@SpringBootTest-context tests are Testcontainers-gated and are skipped when Docker is unavailable, which is exactly why a constructor-injection-breaking change like TrendPullJob's could be committed, merged through five 'repair round' commits (adc9113, 115f698, etc. — this RC's own recent history), and never once fail mvn test in a normal CI run without Docker.
missed_issues.location: No file to cite for an absence; searched for a `@SpringBootTest` class with no `@Testcontainers`/`@Tag("docker")` style guard that asserts `context.getBean(...)` or startup succeeds — none found among the test files under influora-api/src/test/java/com/influora that reference `@SpringBootTest` without also requiring a container.
missed_issues.impact: Every future constructor-injection mistake, missing @Component, or circular-dependency regression on ANY of the ~100+ Spring-managed beans in this service has the same blast radius as EV-001 (total backend outage) and the same near-zero chance of being caught before a production deploy, because the cheapest possible check — 'does the ApplicationContext refresh with an in-memory/H2 or mocked DB' — does not exist as a fast, Docker-free CI gate.
missed_issues.recommended_fix: Add a single `@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = NONE)` smoke test using H2/a mocked DataSource (not Testcontainers) that does nothing but assert the context loads, tagged to run on every `mvn test` (no Docker, no MySQL-only-constraint concerns since it only asserts bean graph wiring, not query behavior). This is the single highest-leverage test this codebase is missing relative to its actual failure history (EV-001 is the second boot-blocking constructor-injection incident referenced in this repo's own project memory).
missed_issues.verification_required: Confirm the new test fails against the pre-fix TrendPullJob (two unannotated constructors) and passes once @Autowired is added, without requiring Docker or a real MySQL instance.
